national.headline: Vice-President releases Vishwasanchar Hindutva Ka
group2: Paper I: AP History & Culture, Indian Constitution, Governance
facts: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan released Vishwasanchar Hindutva Ka, published by Saptahik Vivek, at Vice-President’s Enclave in New Delhi on September 24, 2026.
The release marked the RSS centenary; the organisation was founded by Dr. Keshav Baliram Hedgewar in Nagpur in 1925.
The book examines the movement and exchange of Indian cultural ideas and their interaction with other societies.
national.summary: The book examines cultural exchange and identity in the context of the RSS centenary.
national.staticLink: The RSS was founded in Nagpur, Maharashtra, in 1925 by Dr. Keshav Baliram Hedgewar.
national.prelimsTakeaway: “Vishwasanchar” refers to the global flow and exchange of ideas.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how cultural interaction shapes identities and the interpretation of India’s cultural heritage.

national.headline: Indian Coast Guard conducts ReSAREX-26 off Mumbai
group2: Paper II: Indian Economy, AP Economy, Science & Technology
facts: The Indian Coast Guard held Regional Maritime Search and Rescue Exercise ReSAREX-26 off Mumbai on September 24, 2026.
The exercise tested search-and-rescue procedures, rapid response and coordination between the Coast Guard and Central and State agencies.
Patrol vessels, interceptor boats, Air Cushion Vehicles and helicopters simulated maritime distress situations.
The Indian Coast Guard is under the Ministry of Defence and undertakes maritime search and rescue, coastal security and marine environmental protection.
national.summary: ReSAREX-26 practised coordinated responses to maritime emergencies off the Mumbai coast.
national.staticLink: The Indian Coast Guard was established on February 1, 1977; its motto is “Vayam Rakshamah” (We Protect).
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Indian Coast Guard is India’s nodal agency for maritime search and rescue.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss coordination among maritime and civil agencies in emergency response at sea.

national.canonicalTopic: DRDO Technology Development Fund dilution refrigerator project
national.headline: DRDO signs TDF agreement for indigenous 20-millikelvin dilution refrigerator
facts: On 24 September 2026, DRDO signed a project agreement under the Technology Development Fund with Alwar-based Zero mK India Private Limited.
The project is to develop an indigenous 20-millikelvin dilution refrigerator for quantum applications.
The notes describe the project as the first high-value project under a ₹500-crore corpus for deep-tech and cutting-edge technology projects.
TDF supports industry-led development of indigenous defence and dual-use technologies, particularly by industries, MSMEs and startups.
national.summary: The agreement supports domestic development of a cryogenic system for quantum applications through DRDO’s industry-focused Technology Development Fund.
national.staticLink: A dilution refrigerator is a cryogenic system capable of reaching millikelvin temperatures; 20 mK equals 0.020 Kelvin.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Implementing agency: DRDO; nodal ministry: Ministry of Defence; deep-tech corpus stated in the notes: ₹500 crore.
national.mainsAngle: Industry-led deep-tech support can build domestic capability in quantum technologies and defence-related dual-use research.

sources.title: DRDO Signs First High-Value Deep-Tech Project under TDF

national.notes:
# 1. Agreement
- **Signatories:** **DRDO** and **Zero mK India Private Limited**, an **Alwar**-based company
- **When:** **September 24, 2026**
- **Framework:** Project agreement under the **Technology Development Fund (TDF)**
- **Status:** **MoU signed**
- **Ministry:** **Ministry of Defence**; implementing agency: **DRDO**

# 2. Project and fund
- **Objective:** Develop an indigenous **20-millikelvin dilution refrigerator** for quantum applications
- **Project status:** Described as the first high-value project under a **₹500-crore** corpus for deep-tech and cutting-edge technology projects
- **TDF objective:** Industry-led development of indigenous defence and dual-use technologies, particularly by industries, **MSMEs** and startups
- **Technical fact:** A dilution refrigerator is a cryogenic system capable of reaching millikelvin temperatures; **20 mK = 0.020 Kelvin** [GK]

national.headline: India and the Netherlands sign technical-cooperation MoUs for Gujarat’s Kalpasar project
facts: Two tripartite MoUs were signed during the 9th India International Water Week in New Delhi for technical cooperation and capacity building for Gujarat’s Kalpasar Project.
The partners are the Central Water Commission, Gujarat’s Kalpasar Department, Deltares and Delft University of Technology.
The project envisages an approximately 30-km dam across the Gulf of Khambhat, a freshwater reservoir and irrigation for more than 10 lakh hectares, particularly in Saurashtra.
A proposed road–rail corridor would reduce the Bhavnagar–South Gujarat travel distance to about 60 km; proposed renewable capacity is around 1,500 MW of wind and 1,000 MW of solar power.
national.summary: The MoUs provide for international technical cooperation on Gujarat’s proposed multipurpose water, transport and renewable-energy project. The infrastructure described remains envisaged or proposed.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Kalpasar Project is planned in Gujarat across the Gulf of Khambhat; the MoUs were signed at the 9th India International Water Week in New Delhi.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how international technical cooperation can support integrated water management, irrigation, connectivity and renewable-energy planning.

sources.title: India–Netherlands Agreements for Gujarat’s Kalpasar Project

national.notes:
# 1. MoUs and partners

| Partner | Role in the MoUs |
|---|---|
| **Central Water Commission** | Partner |

| **Deltares** | Partner |
| **Delft University of Technology** | Partner |

# 2. Kalpasar Project
- **Location:** Across the **Gulf of Khambhat**, **Gujarat**
- **Dam:** Approximately **30 km**, envisaged across the gulf

- **Transport:** Proposed road–rail corridor would reduce **Bhavnagar–South Gujarat** travel distance to about **60 km**
- **Renewable capacity proposed:** Around **1,500 MW** of wind power and **1,000 MW** of solar power
